name: TileLang
short: A Python-style language for writing very fast GPU kernels.
what: A Python-style language for writing very fast GPU and CPU code, such as matrix multiplication and FlashAttention. It compiles to CUDA, ROCm, Metal and more.
who: GPU kernel and machine learning systems engineers who already know PyTorch and how GPUs work. It isn't a beginner tool, so most readers will just want to know it exists.
needs: A supported GPU: NVIDIA (the main target), AMD with ROCm, or an Apple Silicon Mac through Metal. The README's quick start uses an NVIDIA GPU

steps.title: On AMD, install a ROCm PyTorch first
steps.code:
pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/rocm7.0
pip install tilelang

try.label: From the README
try.text: Run the README's Quick Start: a short matrix multiply plus ReLU kernel that prints "GEMM + ReLU passed." For a gentler start, the README links examples/quickstart.py and the TileLang Puzzles repo (ten exercises that get harder as you go).

watch: Without a supported GPU, the quick start won't run as written.
Version 0.1.13 removed some older APIs. Read the compatibility notes before upgrading.
The CPU, CuTe DSL and WebGPU backends are experimental.
